section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the three interpretations of "leimar" correspond to three innovations at the Giving of the Torah: the drawing of Atzmus into Torah, the power of Israel to affect G-d, and the Torah's dominion over the world.
section.t: And 4)
Based on this, it can be said that the three matters
(interpretations)
of "leimar" correspond to the three innovations that were introduced at the Giving of the Torah.
For the interpretation of "leimar" in the Giving of the Torah is that an innovation occurred: a person's study of Torah should be with ultimate self-nullification,
in the manner of "my tongue will answer Your word," like one who answers after the reader,
this is from the aspect of the innovation that occurred at the Giving of the Torah regarding the Giver of the Torah.
And as explained above
(section 9)
that the true self-nullification in Torah study comes from the fact that in the Torah given at the Giving of the Torah, there is a drawing down of the Awtsmoos.
And the interpretation of "leimar" that the person learning Torah says to the Holy One, blessed be He, that He should, as it were, repeat His speech,
is from the aspect of the innovation that occurred at the Giving of the Torah regarding Israel, the recipients of the Torah,
that they were given the power to affect, as it were, the Holy One, blessed be He,
"My children have defeated Me, My children have defeated Me."

And the interpretation of "leimar" that the Ten Commandments are drawn from and affect the Ten Utterances is from the aspect of the innovation that occurred at the Giving of the Torah regarding the Torah itself, that it rules and dominates over the world.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section connects the Torah's dominion over the world to the Sages' statement that only one who engages in Torah study is truly free, leading from individual redemption to the ultimate collective redemption.
section.t: And this can be connected with what our Sages, of blessed memory, said,
"There is no free person except for one who engages in the study of Torah,"
for since the Torah rules and dominates over the world,
behold, when one engages in Torah, it is not possible that there should be anyone who rules over him,
for on the contrary,
he rules and dominates over the entire world.
And from the individual redemption
(that through engaging in Torah one becomes free)
we come to the general redemption,
when there will be true freedom,
in the true and complete redemption through our righteous Moshiach, speedily and truly.
